newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB BREWS CRITICAL MASS WITH ROMANIAN BUY.
newsitem.headline: SAB BREWS CRITICAL MASS WITH ROMANIAN BUY.

text.p: South African Breweries Ltd (SAB) said on Wednesday it had consolidated its position in central and eastern Europe with its latest Romanian acquisition, giving the group critical mass in the region.

"We have a very substantial position in central Europe with two breweries in each of Hungary and Poland, and we are market leaders in both countries," chief operating executive Graham Mackay told Reuters.
"Now we have three breweries in Romania which will probably make us the market leader there as well."

The South African concern, which is the world's fourth biggest brewer, announced earlier it had acquired Brau und Brunnen AG's (BUB) controlling interest in two Romanian breweries for an undisclosed amount.
"This positions us very strongly in the whole sub-region, which is really what we have been trying to achieve. The objective was to have a critical mass," said Mackay.

SAB already owns a 70 percent stake in the Vulturul brewery in Romania. The addition of BUB's 73.44 percent shareholding in Ursus SA and its 81.26 percent stake in Pitber SA will make it a leading force in the market.
Ursus has an annual capacity of about 700,000 hectolitres per year, while Pitber is currently being expanded to 750,000.

Mackay said the three beweries together had a market share of around 12 percent last year, and this would increase sharply to around 20 percent over the next year to 18 months as production plant was refurbished and expanded.
There were no immediate plans for further moves in central Europe, Mackay said, adding that the current spread of interests in the region had "a good, solid feel to it".
He declined to say how much SAB paid for the BUB assets but said it would be paying cash for the acquisition, which takes effect from November 1.
The purchase will be funded by proceeds from the group's recent international share offering.
SAB announced earlier this month it was raising $360 million to fund its international expansion, in one of the largest emerging equity issues to international investors by a private sector company.

SAB, which has a 97 percent share of its home market, has placed its international strategic focus on fast-growing emerging and developing drinks markets, entering early in order to gain a dominant position.

Outside Europe, Mackay said the company would continue to invest in new capacity in China, where it has three breweries, as well as in Africa, where it has controlling stakes in breweries in Tanzania, Zambia and Mozambique.
Further small-scale African upgrades and acquisitions were in the pipeline, he added. "There will be some minor announcements coming up in the next couple of months."
